title: 短文写作 · 练习
goal: 在三十分钟内完成切题、展开充分且句子连贯的英语短文。

points.label: 用理由和例子支持中心论点
组成完整且连接正确的句子

sources.title: 全国大学英语四、六级考试大纲（2016年修订版）
sources.used: 材料长度、作答形式与总体评分描述；练习材料为原创。

cards.title: 评分标准：每一档长什么样

levels.name: 13-15 分
levels.summary: 切题，思想表达清楚，文字通顺连贯，基本没有语言错误。
signs: 任务要求完整，论点与例证相互支持。
句间关系清楚，用词和句子结构准确。

levels.name: 10-12 分
levels.summary: 切题，思想表达清楚，文字连贯，只有个别语言错误。
signs: 主要内容完整，理由有必要的解释。
少量语言错误不妨碍理解。

levels.name: 7-9 分
levels.summary: 基本切题，部分意思表达不够清楚，文字勉强连贯，语言错误较多，包含一些严重错误。
signs: 部分理由或例证缺少必要信息。
句子结构或用词错误使部分意思难以理解。

levels.name: 4-6 分
levels.summary: 部分切题，多处意思表达不清，语言错误较多，包含多处严重错误。
signs: 多个句子之间的关系不清楚。

levels.name: 1-3 分
levels.summary: 内容零散，思想表达不清，语言错误严重且频繁。
signs: 只有少量可辨认的相关内容。
很难根据句子理解完整观点。

levels.name: 0 分
levels.summary: 没有可评定的相关英文作答。
signs: 空白、只抄题目或内容与任务无关。

cards.title: 批改单：每次都按这个格式给

format.d: 逐条判：做到了、做了但太薄、没做。每条引用原文中的一句话作依据。
依据总体评分描述判断档次，并说明与本次作答对应的理由。
列出影响理解的语法、用词或衔接错误，给出原句、改法和规则。
选一处展开不足或表达不够清楚的内容，示范怎样补充具体依据。

cards.rules: 按总体表现评价，不给教学反馈维度另设官方分项权重；合理的同义表达不按参考答案的字面形式扣分。 0–5 是对应六个评分档的课程记录值，不是四级报道分。

example.about: 论述大学生参加志愿服务的意义与安排。

coverage.bullet: State your view on volunteering during college.
coverage.quote: Volunteering can be a valuable part of college life, provided that students choose commitments they can manage.
coverage.note: 明确回答大学期间参加志愿服务是否有益，全文立场一致。

coverage.bullet: Support your view with reasons and a specific example.
coverage.quote: For example, a student who helps at a community reading club must explain unfamiliar words clearly and notice when a child needs more time.
coverage.note: 至少展开一条相关理由，并用具体情境说明志愿服务的作用。

coverage.bullet: Suggest how students can balance volunteering with their studies.
coverage.quote: A practical approach is to choose one regular activity, limit the weekly hours, and discuss examination periods with the organizer in advance.
coverage.note: 提出与学习安排相协调的具体做法，说明如何落实。

example.reason: 内容切题，表达清楚，行文通顺连贯，基本没有语言错误。

tasks.purpose: 论述大学生参加志愿服务的意义与安排。
tasks.setting: Your college newspaper is collecting essays about volunteering. Some students worry that regular voluntary work takes time away from study. Write for fellow students about whether volunteering can be a useful part of college life.
tasks.lead: Write an essay of at least 120 words in 30 minutes. In your essay, do the following.
bullets: State your view on volunteering during college.
Support your view with reasons and a specific example.
Suggest how students can balance volunteering with their studies.
must: 明确回答大学期间参加志愿服务是否有益，全文立场一致。
至少展开一条相关理由，并用具体情境说明志愿服务的作用。
提出与学习安排相协调的具体做法，说明如何落实。
tasks.model:
Volunteering can be a valuable part of college life, provided that students choose commitments they can manage. It offers a chance to apply classroom knowledge and understand needs beyond the campus.

For example, a student who helps at a community reading club must explain unfamiliar words clearly and notice when a child needs more time. This experience develops patience and communication skills that cannot be gained simply by reading about them. Working with other volunteers also teaches students to keep promises, since the group depends on everyone arriving as agreed.

However, these benefits do not mean students should accept every request. A practical approach is to choose one regular activity, limit the weekly hours, and discuss examination periods with the organizer in advance. With realistic planning, volunteering can support personal development while leaving enough time for academic work.

tasks.purpose: 分析校园旧物交换中的问题并提出对策。
tasks.setting: A campus picture shows a student throwing a usable desk lamp into a bin while another student nearby is looking at the price of a new lamp. Your college magazine invites comments on this situation.
tasks.lead: Write an essay of at least 120 words in 30 minutes. In your essay, do the following.
bullets: Describe the problem suggested by the picture.
Explain why useful belongings may be thrown away.
Propose a practical way to reduce this waste.
must: 准确概括可用台灯被丢弃而另一人准备购买的反差，不编造人物动机。
解释可用物品未能转给有需要者的一种合理原因，并展开说明。
提出行动主体与操作方式明确的措施，使旧物能到达有需要者手中。
tasks.model:
The picture presents an avoidable waste: one student discards a working lamp while another considers buying a new one. It suggests that useful belongings may be lost when people have no convenient way to pass them on.

Students often move at the end of a term, when packing and examinations leave little time to find buyers. Meanwhile, newcomers may not know that suitable secondhand items are available nearby. The problem is therefore partly a lack of timely information, rather than simply a lack of concern for the environment.

A student association could organize an exchange before the end of each term. Owners would list usable items with clear descriptions, and interested students would arrange collection during fixed hours. Volunteers could check that donated objects are clean and suitable for reuse. By connecting these two groups at the right time, the college could reduce waste and help students avoid unnecessary purchases.
